clue.text: Six stratagems in sneaky codes

blocks.note: VI is six in Roman numerals
ruses are tricks or stratagems

explanation.surface: A spy's half-dozen tricks are tucked away inside secret ciphers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Codes' suggests ciphers, but here it means computer code; the Roman numeral for six opens the word.
explanation.definitionFit: Computer viruses are malicious programs that slip covertly into systems, hence furtive bits of software.

clue.text: Composer is following old king in green coat

indicators.note: following means coming behind, so this piece is placed after the one before it

blocks.note: Giuseppe Verdi, the Italian opera composer
GR stands for Georgius Rex, King George
taken as written

explanation.surface: A musician trails behind an ancient monarch who is dressed in a green jacket.
explanation.walkthrough: The old king is George, whose royal cipher (Georgius Rex) appears on British post boxes; 'coat' here is a surface layer, not clothing.
explanation.definitionFit: Verdigris is the green patina or crust that forms over copper and brass when they weather.

clue.text: British upset about European artisan group ignoring initial reconstruction

indicators.note: to be about something is to surround it, so one piece goes around another
in a down clue, upsetting something turns it upside down, so the letters read bottom to top
ignoring the first letter means leaving the opening letter of the word out

blocks.note: BR is a standard abbreviation for British
E is the abbreviation for European
a guild is a medieval association of craftsmen, here without its first letter

explanation.surface: Britons are upset by a European craft association that skips the first stage of a building project.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'upset' flips the wrapped pair so it reads bottom to top. A guild was a medieval association of craftsmen.
explanation.definitionFit: A rebuild is the noun for a job of reconstructing something, used of engines, houses and teams alike.

clue.text: Soprano leading song about political grouping and health resorts

indicators.note: leading means going in front, so this piece starts the word
something that is about another thing lies all round it, so it encloses it

blocks.note: S is the musical abbreviation for soprano
an aria is a solo song in an opera
the North Atlantic Treaty Organization, a political and military alliance

explanation.surface: A singer leads a protest song about a political alliance and some spa towns.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leading' simply puts the soprano first; ARIA is split around the alliance. The plural is the Latin one.
explanation.definitionFit: Sanatoria, the Latin plural of sanatorium, were institutions where invalids went to recuperate, much like health spas.

clue.text: Informs against drunk looking the worse for wear?

blocks.note: to shop someone is British slang for informing on them to the police
oiled is slang for intoxicated

explanation.surface: Someone grasses on a drinker who already looks a wreck.
explanation.walkthrough: To 'shop' someone is British slang for informing on them; 'oiled' is slang for drunk.
explanation.definitionFit: Shop-soiled goods have become faded or grubby from being on display, so they look worn and past their best.

clue.text: Pub storing a lot of booze? That’s making sense

indicators.note: a lot of something is most but not all of it, so the final letter is dropped
storing means holding inside, so one piece sits within the other

blocks.note: a local is the British name for one's neighbourhood pub
gin, a common spirit, without its final letter

explanation.surface: A pub stocks plenty of drink, which seems perfectly sensible.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'local' is the British term for one's regular neighbourhood pub; most of GIN goes inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Something logical follows reason and is coherent, so it is sensible or makes sense.

clue.text: Verse, after initial line, a source of precious stuff?

indicators.note: an initial is the first letter of a word, so only the opening letter is kept
coming after places one piece behind the other in sequence

blocks.note: the first letter of the word
an ode is a lyric poem, a piece of verse

explanation.surface: A poet wonders whether a poem, once past its opening line, becomes a treasure.
explanation.walkthrough: The verse comes second in the answer despite coming first in the clue, because 'after' places it behind the letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A lode is a vein of metal ore in rock, which miners follow to extract gold or silver.

clue.text: Bird’s head seen amongst half the bushes etc? This is a diving bird

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter
taking half of a word discards the remaining letters
something seen amongst other things sits in their midst

blocks.note: the opening letter of the word
greenery covers bushes and other plants; only its first half is kept

explanation.surface: A birdwatcher glimpses a head among the shrubs and identifies a diving species.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The bushes etc' stands for greenery; its first four letters take the B inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Grebes are freshwater birds that dive underwater to catch fish, famous for elaborate courtship displays.

clue.text: Musical instrument in case, seen in church area

indicators.note: being seen in a place means sitting inside it

blocks.note: CE is the Church of England
lest means in case, as in 'lest we forget'
A is the abbreviation for area

explanation.surface: An instrument in its carrying case is spotted somewhere in a church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In case' looks like a carrying case but is the conjunction, as in 'lest we forget'.
explanation.definitionFit: The celesta is a keyboard instrument striking metal plates, famous for the Sugar Plum Fairy dance.

clue.text: British writer depressed over really vacuous British painter too

indicators.note: vacuous means empty, so the inside of the word is emptied and only its ends remain
in a down clue, being over something means sitting above it, so it comes first

blocks.note: feeling low is feeling depressed
just the outside letters of the word

explanation.surface: A gloomy British novelist sits above an empty-headed British artist.
explanation.walkthrough: The surname serves twice: Malcolm Lowry wrote Under the Volcano, and L. S. Lowry painted matchstick figures in industrial Lancashire.
explanation.definitionFit: Two famous Britons share this surname: novelist Malcolm and the painter of northern mill towns.

clue.text: Wood goblin lore possibly encompasses fine woodland sprite

indicators.note: to encompass is to surround, so the other letters are taken around one more
possibly signals one possible arrangement among many, so the letters may be rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written
F is the pencil-grading abbreviation for fine

explanation.surface: Folk tales about forest goblins feature an elfin spirit of the woods.
explanation.walkthrough: All fifteen letters of the first three words plus F are rearranged; the surface makes it look like a straight description.
explanation.definitionFit: Robin Goodfellow is another name for Puck, the mischievous fairy of English folklore and A Midsummer Night's Dream.

clue.text: Old foolish state? It’s uncomfortably seen in way of speaking

indicators.note: sitting uncomfortably means being out of place, so the letters are disarranged
being seen in something means being found inside it

blocks.note: taken as written, apostrophe dropped
an idiom is a characteristic mode of expression

explanation.surface: Someone muses that old-fashioned silliness sits awkwardly in a particular turn of phrase.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It's' looks like the start of a new sentence but is fodder; 'way of speaking' is IDIOM, which ironically is another meaning of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiotism is an archaic word for idiocy, the condition of being foolish; 'Old' flags that the sense is dated.

clue.text: Material considered new in the US?

blocks.note: first meaning: a soft knitted fabric
second meaning: the Channel Island whose name, over in America, gets 'New' attached as a state

explanation.walkthrough: Jersey in the Channel Islands has an American namesake, the state of New Jersey; across the Atlantic the name is thus 'considered new'.
explanation.definitionFit: Jersey is a stretchy knitted fabric named after the island, and the US state carries the same name with New prefixed.

clue.text: Church ledge near person, one with binder?

blocks.note: near is old slang for stingy, so a near person is a miser
I is the Roman numeral for one
a cord is something used to tie or bind

explanation.surface: A church shelf sits next to someone holding a ring binder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Near' looks like a word of position but means mean with money; 'with' simply joins I to the binding string.
explanation.definitionFit: A misericord is a small projecting ledge under a hinged choir seat, giving standing clergy something to lean against.

clue.text: Republican Party brought back the cane

indicators.note: bringing something back returns it the way it came, so the letters run right to left

blocks.note: R is the abbreviation for Republican
a do is an informal word for a party

explanation.surface: Hardline Republicans revive corporal punishment in schools.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brought back' fits the surface story of reinstating punishment, but it turns the party word round.
explanation.definitionFit: The rod and the cane both mean corporal punishment with a stick, as in 'spare the rod'.

clue.text: Fruit profit involves Conservative getting very angry

indicators.note: to involve is to include within, so one piece is taken inside another

blocks.note: a raisin is a dried grape
a gain is a profit
C is the abbreviation for Conservative

explanation.surface: A fruit company's profits make a Tory boardroom member furious.
explanation.walkthrough: The C slips in after the first letter of GAIN; Conservative is the British right-of-centre party.
explanation.definitionFit: Raising Cain is an idiom for causing an uproar or creating a furious fuss, after the biblical murderer.

clue.text: Nasty egotist we learn about

indicators.note: something nasty is twisted and spoiled, so the letters are mangled into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: We discover something unpleasant about a self-centred person.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nasty' reads as an adjective on the egotist, but it is the signal to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: To get wise to something is an informal idiom for becoming aware of it or finding out about it.

clue.text: Lingerie item getting no exclamation? Chap paying insufficient attention

indicators.note: getting none of something means it is lost from the word

blocks.note: a negligee is a flimsy dressing gown
gee is an exclamation of surprise; this is the part removed
a gent is a man or chap

explanation.surface: A man is so distracted he doesn't even exclaim at some lingerie.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gee' is the exclamation removed from the end of NEGLIGEE.
explanation.definitionFit: A negligent person fails to take proper care, which is to say they are careless or inattentive.

clue.text: Unchanged admin trainee accepting employment? It’s being put through the grinder

definitions.text: It’s being put through the grinder

indicators.note: to accept something is to take it in, so one piece goes inside another

blocks.note: unchanged means the same
usage is the employment or use of something
the first letters of Administration Trainee, an old British civil-service grade

explanation.surface: A junior office worker takes a job and is put through the mill, while staying exactly as before.
explanation.walkthrough: Administration Trainee was the old fast-stream entry grade of the British civil service. The definition sounds like an ordeal but is meant literally.
explanation.definitionFit: Sausagemeat is minced meat, produced literally by feeding it through a mincer; the definition plays on the idiom for an ordeal.

clue.text: Swedish city in revolt, regrettably uprising in pursuit of power

indicators.note: in a down clue, rising means reading from the bottom upwards
to be in pursuit of something is to follow behind it

blocks.note: up in arms, so people in revolt are up
P is the abbreviation for power
alas expresses regret

explanation.surface: A Swedish city erupts in rebellion, a regrettable uprising seeking power.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Uprising' fits the revolution story, but in a down clue it means reading upward. 'Up in arms' explains why rebels are up.
explanation.definitionFit: Uppsala is a university city north of Stockholm and one of the oldest towns in Sweden.

clue.text: Trouser gossip with a twist

indicators.note: giving something a twist turns it around, so the letters face the other way

blocks.note: to gab is to chatter or gossip

explanation.surface: Some chatter about trousers, delivered with a twist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trouser' looks like a noun about clothing but is the verb meaning to pocket something.
explanation.definitionFit: To trouser and to bag are both informal verbs for grabbing or pocketing something for yourself.

clue.text: Underwear source of vulgar fuss and swagger

indicators.note: the source of a word is where it starts, its first letter

blocks.note: a bra is an item of underwear
the opening letter of the word
ado means fuss, as in much ado about nothing

explanation.surface: Underwear causes a crude commotion and a show of cockiness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'And' is a link word here, joining the wordplay to the definition at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Bravado is a boastful show of boldness, much the same as a confident strut.

clue.text: Heads for the old excellent Astaire-Rogers film

indicators.note: the heads of words are their first letters

blocks.note: first letters of both words
phat is slang for excellent

explanation.surface: A nostalgic call to seek out a wonderful old Fred and Ginger musical.
explanation.walkthrough: The split ignores the word break: the heads give two letters and the slang word supplies the remaining four. Phat is hip-hop slang for excellent.
explanation.definitionFit: Top Hat is the 1935 musical starring Fred Astaire and Ginger Rogers, featuring 'Cheek to Cheek'.

clue.text: Bill left with a set of drums

blocks.note: a tab is a bill, as at a bar
L is the abbreviation for left
taken as written

explanation.surface: Bill goes off, leaving behind a drum kit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bill' looks like a man's name but is the bill you run up at a bar.
explanation.definitionFit: The tabla is a pair of hand drums used in Indian classical music, played together as one instrument.

clue.text: New kids initially seen in beer joint

indicators.note: initially means at the start, so each word gives only its first letter
something seen in a place sits within it

blocks.note: ale is a type of beer
first letters of both words

explanation.surface: Underage youngsters are spotted in a pub serving beer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Joint' looks like a bar or dive to go with the beer, but it is a body part.
explanation.definitionFit: The ankle is the hinge where the foot meets the leg, one of the body's joints.

clue.text: Mountaineer finally a bit misguided, probing K2 in quite the wrong country

indicators.note: finally points to the last letter of the word
misguided means led astray, so these letters go the wrong way
a probe pushes into something, so this goes inside

blocks.note: K with 2 written as Roman II
the last letter of the word
the four letters rearranged

explanation.surface: A climber, slightly lost, explores K2 but finds himself in entirely the wrong nation.
explanation.walkthrough: K2 becomes K plus Roman II; R and the rearranged letters go between the two Is. K2 is in the Himalayas, but this nation is low Pacific atolls.
explanation.definitionFit: Kiribati is a Pacific island republic of flat coral atolls, about as far from a towering Himalayan peak as possible.

clue.text: Famous performer’s fixed look, dropping tab

indicators.note: to drop something is to let it fall away, so a letter is lost

blocks.note: a stare is a fixed gaze
a tab of E, slang for an ecstasy tablet

explanation.surface: A celebrity's glassy gaze suggests they have taken a pill.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'tab' is a tablet of the drug ecstasy, known as E; that letter goes from the end of the gaze.
explanation.definitionFit: A star is a celebrated actor or entertainer, a leading celebrity of stage or screen.

clue.text: Lapse in concentration and so on - too old for the job? It’s seen everywhere

definitions.note: a clue-as-sentence description of the noun phrase

blocks.note: a blank is a moment when the mind goes empty
etc, short for et cetera
over age, past the limit

explanation.surface: An ageing worker's lapses suggest they are past it, and everybody notices.
explanation.walkthrough: The pieces ignore the word break, with the abbreviation for 'and so on' straddling both words; read the last piece as 'over age'.
explanation.definitionFit: Blanket coverage reaches every place or case without exception, so it is found all over.

clue.text: American adult shifting energy in a superficial way?

definitions.note: adverbial phrase; the answer is the adjective as in 'an amateur effort'

indicators.note: shifting means moving to a new place, so one letter is relocated within the word

blocks.note: A is the abbreviation for American
mature means fully grown

explanation.surface: A grown-up American changes jobs and works only half-heartedly.
explanation.walkthrough: Only the E moves, two places along, so this is a minimal rearrangement rather than a full mix.
explanation.definitionFit: Amateur work is unskilled or dabbling, done without professional depth, hence superficial.

clue.text: Withdraw doctor: operation unacceptable

blocks.note: Dr is the abbreviation for doctor
op is short for operation
out means not allowed, as in that's out

explanation.surface: A patient pulls out, declaring the surgeon's proposed procedure unacceptable.
explanation.walkthrough: The colon makes it look like a medical story, but each word just supplies a short piece.
explanation.definitionFit: To drop out is to withdraw from a course or competition before finishing it.
